Nice post. Unsatisfying conclusion - did you ever figure out why the original adapter was throttled when plugged into the monitor, and not when plugged into the computer?

archerx · Nov 21, 2026

I’m guessing it’s a USB bandwidth issue. I learned about these kind of limitations when I tried to have 3 kinects running at the same time on the same USB bus.

KeplerBoy · Nov 21, 2026

He states that high speed SSDs through the monitor are fine though.

swiftcoder · Nov 21, 2026

> I’m guessing it’s a USB bandwidth issue

It's explicitly not a bandwidth issue (that would also affect the SSD). It's a latency issue - the chip doesn't have a big enough buffer to keep sufficient packets in flight at once.

cibyr · Nov 21, 2026

The additional latency from going through the monitor made the bandwidth-delay product exceed the amount of data the adapter was able to send before receiving an ack. I thought that was fairly clear from the explanation, but now I notice that he didn't mention the latency without the monitor.

ferdzo · Nov 21, 2026

I've encountered a similar problem, the wifi on a MacBook Air was dying once connected to a Dell monitor over USB-C. The wifi signal was going from full to nearly no signal. Connecting to the same monitor with a dongle and HDMI didn't have the same outcome. Never had a time to find the culprit. Probably EMI or bad grounding.
